faq.q: Why are Indian mutual funds no longer accepting fresh investments in global funds?
faq.a: Many Indian mutual funds halted fresh investments into global schemes because the industry collectively approached or breached the overseas investment limits set by the RBI and SEBI, necessitating a temporary pause on new inflows.

faq.q: What is the RBI's LRS limit for global investments?
faq.a: The RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) allows resident Indian individuals to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year (April 1 to March 31) for various purposes, including direct investments in foreign assets.

faq.q: What are UCITS ETFs and why are they relevant for Indian investors?
faq.a: UCITS ETFs are Exchange Traded Funds regulated under a strict European Union framework, known for investor protection and transparency. They are relevant for Indian investors as they offer a regulated, cost-effective, and diversified way to gain direct exposure to global markets, especially after restrictions on Indian global mutual funds.

faq.q: How are dividends and capital gains from global investments taxed in India?
faq.a: Dividends are taxed as 'Income from Other Sources' at your slab rates. Short-Term Capital Gains (held < 24 months) are taxed at slab rates, while Long-Term Capital Gains (held > 24 months) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.

faq.q: Is TCS applicable on remittances for global investments?
faq.a: Yes, a Tax Collected at Source (TCS) of 20% is applicable on LRS remittances exceeding ₹7 lakhs in a financial year for investment purposes. This is an advance tax that can be claimed as a credit against your total tax liability.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) invest in UCITS ETFs?
faq.a: NRIs are generally not subject to LRS limits as they are not resident Indians. They can typically invest in UCITS ETFs through international brokerage accounts, subject to the regulations of their country of residence and the brokerage firm.
